svg.title: Grids that scale 01 · The rule (amendment 3)
svg.text: Collections are one auto-fill grid with the shared class; panels sit in bands; wide pages stop at 120 rem. Numbers at a 16 px rem.
One pattern, three sizes: the card count follows the width
repeat(auto-fill, minmax(min(100%, var(--canccu-grid-min)), 1fr)), gap 1 rem (tiles 0.5 rem). Each strip is the
Wide screens: columns keep coming up to 120 rem of content
From 1100 px the menu takes 16 rem and the side padding is 2.5 rem. A wide page's content stops at 120 rem (1,920
px, the dashed line) and keeps the one left edge: at 2560 px and on an ultra-wide the rest stays empty, so the crew's
eye never travels more than a 1920 screen's width and the counts match the venue's own 1920 screens.
Unequal heights: rows align, no masonry
Rows align; actions at the foot
An organiser reads a row across: zone beside
zone, sound beside sound. Rows that align keep
the reading order left to right, and every
card's buttons line up at the row's foot.
Masonry places a card under the shortest
column, so its place depends on the heights
above it. When a zone gets one more waiting
moment live, the cards after it change
columns while the crew aims at them.
A card's own list shows at most 4 rows, then
“+n more”, so no card is far taller than its
Panels go in bands above or below, never in a column beside
Above the collection: the page's crew
actions (one band, one row on a desk),
then its summary and filters. Below it:

Only a master–detail page has a column

Few and none: one or two keep their width
auto-fill keeps the empty tracks, so a single card at 1920 px is 304 px wide, at the one left edge. auto-fit would
stretch it across 1,584 px. None: the shared empty state (icon, title, one sentence, the main action) replaces the
Phone: one column, crew actions first
Under about 37 rem of content every card grid is one column; small items keep two and tiles
three. The page's order is the phone's order, so a reader and a screen reader meet crew actions
Fixed columns stay where the layout means it
Each one is marked in its CSS with its kind and reason (canccu-grid: fixed <kind> — <why>), so the guard lets it through and a reviewer sees why.
